title: Microburst fusion: latency vs cost canvas
content:
Executive summary:

This sketch documents a small bench exploring a 'fusion' approach to microburst handling: combine short-lived warm slots, opportunistic tiling, and a thin handshake bypass to reduce p90/p99 in microbursty interactive workloads while keeping $/1k tokens modest. This is intentionally lightweight (lab-grade) and focused on conversational micro-interactions (5-30 tokens per turn) typical of in-product chat UIs.

Motivation / hypothesis:
- Microbursts (10s-100s qps for <200ms) dominate real world interactive tail pain.
- Pure prewarm or always-on slots cost too much; pure on-demand cold starts kill p99.
- Fusion: route tiny bursts to ephemeral warm slots (fast wake) + sliding-tiling multiplexing to amortize kernel setup; expect p90 improvement with <20% $ uplift vs on-demand.

Testbed and methodology:
- Hardware: 2x A100-80GB (host pool), 2x L4x (edge-pop emulation) — results reported per-GPU equivalence.
- Models: Llama-3-8b-quant (4-bit), OpenLlama-13b-fp16 (baseline heavy), lightweight distilled-3b-compact (low-cost variant).
- Runtime flags: windowed-tiling=true, handshake-bypass=experimental, prefetch-kv=on, slot-timeout=350ms.
- Workloads: three canonical microburst profiles (see below). Each run: 30m steady-state with repeated randomized bursts, 20 repeats per profile.
- Metrics captured: qps, p50/p90/p99 latency (server-side decode start), token-throughput, cost proxy = amortized GPU-minutes per 1k tokens (internal burn model).

Workload profiles (sketch):
- profile-A (needle): 1s spike 150 reqs -> 0 for 9s (10s cadence), mean turn 12 tokens.
- profile-B (wave): 5s at 60 reqs/sec -> 30s lull, mean turn 18 tokens.
- profile-C (sputter): continuous low qps with occasional 500ms microspikes of 80 reqs.

Representative numeric summary (per-GPU equiv):

ASCII table:
| profile | model                 | qps-peak | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | $/1k-tokens | notes |
|---------|-----------------------|----------:|--------:|--------:|--------:|-----------:|-------|
| A       | llama-3-8b-quant      |     150   |     38  |    115  |    410  |     1.12   | baseline on-demand cold penalty visible
| A       | llama-3-8b-quant (fusion) | 150   |     34  |     86  |    210  |     1.28   | fusion reduces p90/p99 substantially, +14% cost
| B       | distilled-3b-compact  |      60   |     22  |     68  |    160  |     0.48   | cheap but p99 stretched in sustained waves
| B       | distilled-3b-compact (fusion) | 60 |  20  |     48  |    102  |     0.55   | good p90 with small cost hit
| C       | openllama-13b-fp16    |      80   |     46  |    160  |    520  |     2.40   | heavy model shows tail sensitivity
| C       | openllama-13b-fp16 (fusion) | 80 |  41  |    112  |    300  |     2.60   | tail improves, cost up ~8%

Interpretation notes:
- Fusion most effective for profile-A (short, dense needles) where ephemeral warm slots are reused across closely spaced requests.
- For longer sustained bursts (profile-B) fusion still helps but amortization points differ: tiling and multiplex settings need tuning to avoid slot thrash.
- Heavy models see absolute p99 reductions but relative cost uplift is smaller because baseline $/1k is already high.
- Distilled/compact variants pair well with fusion for cost-sensitive tiers: modest cost uplift yields large latency improvements.

Micro-observations and traces (hand snippets):
- Handshake overhead: baseline 1.8ms median for L4x; 1.2ms with bypass enabled (experimental). Bypass occasionally shows a 50-100ms outlier during contention — plausible race with prefetch.
- Slot lifetime distribution (fusion): 80% of ephemeral slots reclaimed within 420ms; 12% lasted 1-2s due to back-to-back contextual sessions.
- KV-prefetch hit: profile-A saw 62% cache hit on fusion path vs 18% baseline (explains p90 improvement).

Small ASCII sparkline (p90 over time for single run, profile-A, llama-3-8b-quant):
[time] 0------10------20------30m
[p90]  120/110/95/92/86/88/90/110/130/95/
(note: coarse samples every 3 minutes)

Actionable tuning knobs to try next:
- slot-timeout sweep: 200ms, 350ms, 700ms — we suspect 200ms aggressive reclaim reduces cost but can hurt p99 for returning sessions.
- tiling-window micro-bench: 5ms vs 15ms vs 40ms; smaller window favors latency at the expense of packing efficiency.
- handshake-bypass fallback heuristics: only apply when client RTT < 40ms and model quantized.
- hybrid routing: send first token to compact model on fusion path; if continued conversation >32 tokens, stitch to larger model with KV transfer (stitchback).

Open questions / unknowns:
- How well does fusion generalize across multitenant noisy hosts? Our lab used synthetic isolation; real customer noisy neighbors could reduce ephemeral slot reuse.
- Interaction with autoscaling: does rapid creation of ephemeral slots cause autoscaler churn? initial signs: small spike in placement ops but within tolerable range for our test autoscaler.
- Billing attribution complexity: need to attribute ephemeral warm-slot minutes cleanly to tenant to avoid surprise invoices.

Next steps (proposal):
1) Run a controlled 48h cluster-level run with noisy-background tenants (simulate 30% noise) to validate stability.
2) Sweep slot-timeout and tiling-window to create a small Pareto frontier chart of p90 vs $/1k for our three model classes.
3) Prototype a conservative handshake-bypass circuit breaker (samples fallback on first k runs) and measure fallbacks per 10k sessions.
4) Draft a one-pager for product that maps fusion benefits to common Redwood customer personas (consumer chat, internal assistant, search-snap).

Appendix: raw run notes (selected)
- run 2029-06-12-11AM: profile-A, fusion on, observed 28% reduction in p90 vs baseline for llama-3-8b-quant; KV-prefetch accounted for 14% of that improvement.
- run 2029-06-13-09PM: profile-C with noisy background, slot reclaiming thrash increased by 3x causing brief p95 spikes ~200ms.

Author notes / artifacts to link:
- Quick trace snippets saved to GH gist (link in JIRA).
- Confluence draft for tuning guidelines: CONFLUENCE-3152.

This doc is a working sketch: informal notes, not yet validated across production multitenant runs. Feedback welcome, especially on experiments to stress autoscaler and billing attribution.
